final_text:
T3 is done, passing on the first execution.

**Approach:** a plain script on `torch` + `safetensors`, with sharding delegated to `huggingface_hub.split_torch_state_dict_into_shards` — the same splitter `transformers.save_pretrained` uses, so the layout and `weight_map` are canonical HF rather than hand-rolled. I skipped `save_pretrained` itself despite `F-allowed.md` suggesting it for T3: it applies one global dtype and cannot express per-tensor mixed precision.

**Targeting:** the 64 projection names are built explicitly from `range(16) × 4 suffixes`, never by regex — a `.*weight` pattern would have swept in the embeddings and every layer norm. The 48 dropped buffers are likewise an explicit list, which matters because `attention.bias` (uint8 causal mask) looks exactly like a projection bias next to `attention.dense.bias`, which must survive as float32.

**Result** — `out/T3/`, 9 shards + index, 196 tensors:

| | |
|---|---|
| bfloat16 | 64 (exactly the projections) |
| float32 | 132 |
| shards 1–2 | `embed_out` / `embed_in`, 412 MB each, alone (fp32 puts them well over budget) |
| shards 3–9 | 15–33 tensors, max 260,317,184 B — under the 268,435,456 B budget |

All four required checks run before anything is written and exit loudly on failure, plus guards for no-match, over-match (the non-fp32 set must *equal* the 64 projections), dropping a parameter, and per-shard budget. I then re-read the written shards independently: every tensor is bit-exact against the source cast to its target dtype, and `weight_map` resolves correctly for all 196.

Two things the task text left open, noted in `out/T3/REPORT.md`: shard file naming (I used HF's `model-0000N-of-00009.safetensors`) and whether config/tokenizer files should be copied (I wrote only shards + index, per "Required result"). Also worth flagging — the text quotes the embeddings as "206 MB each", which is their float16 *input* size; in the float32 output they're 412 MB.
